name: Tamatiebredie
summary: Tomato and lamb stew: bone-in lamb and potatoes braised slowly until the tomatoes collapse into a thick, sweet-sour red gravy.
about: Bredie is the Cape word for a slow stew of meat and vegetables, and the tomato version is the best known. It belongs to both Cape Malay and Afrikaans home cooking, made in winter when a pot can sit on the stove all afternoon, and served over white rice.

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and chopped, or 2 x 400 g tins chopped tomatoes

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: more if the tomatoes are sour

steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in two batches, about 4 minutes a side, until well coloured. Lift it out onto a plate.
Turn the heat to medium, add the onions to the fat in the pot and fry, stirring, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, cinnamon stick, cloves and bay leaves and fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and water, scraping up the brown bits on the bottom. Return the lamb and its juices, season with salt and pepper, and bring to the boil.
Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring now and then so nothing catches. The tomatoes should break down into a sauce.

Add the potatoes and chilli flakes, pushing the potatoes under the sauce. Cover and simmer for another 40 to 45 minutes, until the lamb pulls easily from the bone and a knife slides through the potatoes.

Take the lid off for the last 10 minutes if the gravy is thin; it should be thick enough to coat a spoon. Taste, add salt or a pinch of sugar, fish out the cinnamon and bay leaves, and serve over white rice.
prepNote: Even better the next day: cool, refrigerate overnight, lift off the fat and reheat gently.
